skill.name: perigon-angular
skill.description: Angular 21+ standalone/Material/signal conventions for Perigon WebApp
skill.summary: Angular 21+ standalone/Material/signal conventions for Perigon WebApp
skill.author: AterDev

security_audit.summary: Static findings were false positives caused by Angular guidance using words like standalone, signals, and tooling. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or unsafe command execution was found in SKILL.md.

static_findings.snippet: - Components: standalone only; avoid NgModules. Use Angular Material; theming in styles.scss/theme.s
- State/forms: prefer signals and signal forms; avoid legacy two-way binding when signals suffice.
- Tooling: use pnpm; avoid builds/tests unless requested. Keep ESLint/tsconfig defaults; prefer stan

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 10 describes Angular component conventions, including standalone components and local stylesheet placement. It does not request host discovery, environment probing, or other reconnaissance.
Line 11 gives Angular state and form style guidance about signals and binding. It contains no instruction to inspect system details or collect sensitive information.

Line 15 gives project tooling preferences for pnpm, lint configuration, and Angular Material imports. The note about builds and tests limits routine work scope, not security review or system reconnaissance.

content.value_statement: Angular teams need consistent project conventions across routes, services, UI, styles, and i18n. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code toward Perigon WebApp patterns.
actual_capabilities: Guides work in src/ClientApp/WebApp for components, routes, services, styles, and i18n.
Promotes standalone Angular components instead of NgModules.
Directs UI work toward Angular Material and project theme files.
Encourages signals and signal forms for state and form handling.
Points API client work to app/services and existing environment configuration.
Keeps localization keys aligned with assets/i18n and shared i18n key files.
limitations: It does not generate Angular code by itself.
It does not document backend API behavior.
It assumes the Perigon WebApp folder layout exists.
It does not replace project tests or code review.

use_cases.title: Add Angular Pages
use_cases.description: Create or update WebApp pages while following Perigon route, layout, style, and component locations.

use_cases.title: Maintain Shared UI
use_cases.description: Build shared Angular Material components with standalone imports and local stylesheet conventions.

use_cases.title: Align Localization Work
use_cases.description: Update translated strings and keys while keeping assets and shared i18n references consistent.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Page
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new WebApp page.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Perigon Angular page for [feature]. Follow the app/pages layout, standalone component style, Angular Material usage, and local SCSS conventions.

prompt_templates.title: Update a Service
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for API client changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Update the Angular service for [API area]. Keep client files in app/services, preserve the HTTP interceptor, and use existing environment configuration.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor State
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for modern Angular state handling.
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor [component or form] to use signals or signal forms where appropriate. Preserve behavior and avoid legacy two-way binding unless needed.

prompt_templates.title: Review Feature Fit
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review before merging frontend work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Angular change for Perigon conventions. Check routes, layout reuse, Material imports, services, i18n keys, auth guards, and stylesheet placement.

output_examples.input: Add an admin settings page to the WebApp.
output_examples.output: A concise implementation plan that places the page under app/pages, uses standalone Angular Material imports, and updates routing consistently.

output_examples.input: Review a pull request that adds translated labels.
output_examples.output: A review summary that checks assets/i18n files, shared key references, and user-facing text consistency.

output_examples.input: Modernize an Angular form in a Perigon component.
output_examples.output: A refactor plan that uses signals where suitable, preserves validation behavior, and keeps styles beside the component.

best_practices: Keep new UI work inside the existing WebApp folder structure.
Use standalone components and Angular Material imports that match nearby files.
Update i18n keys and translated strings together.
anti_patterns: Do not introduce NgModules for new components.
Do not bypass the existing customer HTTP interceptor.
Do not scatter page styles outside the component stylesheet pattern.

faq.question: What projects is this skill for?
faq.answer: It is for frontend work in the Perigon WebApp Angular application.

faq.question: Does it require Angular Material?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance prefers Angular Material and the existing theme files.

faq.question: Can it help with services?
faq.answer: Yes. It directs HTTP clients, models, and service files to app/services.

faq.question: Does it cover localization?
faq.answer: Yes. It points string work to assets/i18n files and shared key references.

faq.question: Should tests run automatically?
faq.answer: No. The skill says to avoid builds or tests unless the user requests them.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
